entry.title: The Merck/Moderna Results
entry.summary:
This is one of those times - and there are many - when you should evaluate a biopharma news story based on the science and not on the stock market. I’m referring to the clinical trial data that Merck and Moderna released yesterday for their vaccine (intismeran autogene)/Keytruda combination in melanoma patients after surgery. That should probably read “released under duress”, because the data leaked in advance of a meeting presentation, and the companies were more or less forced to press-release on the numbers.

Source: In the Pipeline (Derek Lowe — Drug Discovery & Chemistry) · Tags: #genomics-proteins #materials-science

entry.title: flodl-bio: First Rust data, transformers and model layer for entire deep learning on biological sequences
entry.summary:
Python ecosystem dominates the deep learning framework. flodl-bio is a Rust crate that extends flodl, a libtorch-backed deep-learning framework, with deep learning on biological sequences. To our knowledge, flodl-bio is the first Rust crate that provides a comprehensive and practical deep learning for the biological applications, which includes the alphabet-aware sequence encoding, including one-hot and k-mer representations, padded sequences, and channels-first batches.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01073-y Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #genomics-proteins

entry.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01062-1 This study presents HDOCK-Multimer, a general framework for structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
